ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is a point on the line $AB$, $\angle AOC=50^\circ$, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOC$, and $\angle DOE=90^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOD$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOD + \angle BOD = 180^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOD = 180^\circ - \angle AOD = \boxed{155^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is a point on the line $AB$, $\angle AOC=50^\circ$, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOC$, and $\angle DOE=90^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOD$ in degrees?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Since $\angle AOD + \angle BOD = 180^\circ$, it follows that $\angle BOD = 180^\circ - \angle AOD = \boxed{155^\circ}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is a horizontal straight line, point O is on straight line AB, A is to the left of O, and B is to the right of O, so rays OA and OB are opposite rays. In the figure, there are also rays OC, OD, and OE starting from O, among which OC and OD are both above straight line AB and toward the left, and OD is located inside the angle formed by OA and OC; OE is above straight line AB and toward the right. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOC = 50°, and OD bisects ∠AOC, so ∠AOD = 50° ÷ 2 = 25°. Since OA and OB are opposite rays on a straight line, ∠AOD and ∠BOD form a pair of linear angles, and their sum is 180°. Therefore ∠BOD = 180° − 25° = 155°.
